r1.why: Trichromacy for most humans [3], bees/UV and different cone counts [4], cone sensitivity processed by brain [5].

r2.why: Wavelength and intensity [17], 390-700 nm visible light [18], spectrum as intensity per wavelength [19].

r3.why: More spectra than sensations [20], color as class of spectra varying by species/individual [21], metamers [22], metamerism [8].

r4.why: Single-wavelength rainbow colors and Newton 1671 Latin naming [24], 100% purity [26], cultural division [28], ROYGBIV dispute over indigo/cyan [29].

r5.why: Absorb/scatter [36], transparent colorless [38], opaque [39], translucent internal scattering [40], heat [41].

r6.why: Intensity relative to context [31], brown/olive examples [32], Bezold-Brucke shift [33].

r7.why: Additive/subtractive mixing [7], color space and model [9], reproduction uses [10], named models [11].
